style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">consistent with the overall</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">growth of</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the business,</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">and a $1.0 million increase in prepaid</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">expenses.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Investing Activities</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our investing activities consist primarily of purchases, sales and maturities of available-for-sale securities, property and equipment purchases for computer-related equipment, leasehold improvements to leased office facilities and capitalization of software development costs. Capitalized software development costs are related to new applications or improvements to our existing software platform that expands the functionality for internal use software.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net cash used in investing activities during 2017 consisted primarily of $69.2 million in purchases of available-for-sale securities, and $3.6 million of purchased property and equipment and capitalized software development costs, offset by $50.5 million of cash maturities from available-for-sale securities.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net cash used in investing activities during 2016 consisted primarily of $75.3 million in purchases of available-for-sale securities, and $5.4 million of purchased property and equipment and capitalized software development costs, offset by $6.2 million of cash maturities from available-for-sale securities.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net cash provided<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>by investing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>activities during 2015 was $6.7 million,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>consisting<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>primarily of $16.8 million<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>cash maturities<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>available-for-sale<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>securities, offset<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>by $7.6<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>million<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>purchased property<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and equipment and capitalized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>software<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>development<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>costs,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and $2.7 million<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in purchases of available-for-sale<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>securities.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Financing Activities</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our financing activities consist primarily of proceeds from the exercise of stock options, proceeds from purchases of Class A common stock under our employee stock purchase plan, proceeds from our IPO and debt borrowings to fund our operations. Cash flows used in financing activities consist primarily of payment of IPO costs, repayment of capital leases and repayment of debt borrowings.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net cash provided by financing activities for 2017 consisted primarily of $21.9 million from proceeds received from option exercises and $4.4 million from proceeds from the purchase of Class A common stock under the employee stock purchase plan, offset by the repayment of $0.2 million in payment of IPO costs.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net cash provided by financing activities for 2016 consisted primarily of $102.7 million of IPO proceeds, net of underwriting discounts, $20.0 million in principal proceeds from term loan borrowings and $1.3 million from proceeds received from option exercises, offset by the repayment of $20.0 million in principal payments on term loan borrowings, and payment of IPO costs and loan fees of $2.4 million.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net cash provided<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>by financing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>activities for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>2015 consisted primarily of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>$2.7 million<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of proceeds received from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>option exercises, offset<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>by the payment of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>IPO costs of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>$1.1 million.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Contractual Obligations and Commitments</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2017, our principal obligations consisted of obligations under non-cancellable operating leases that expire at various dates through 2023. Purchase obligations include certain other non-cancellable agreements for software and marketing services that specify all significant terms, including fixed or minimum services to be used, pricing provisions and the approximate timing of the transaction. Obligations under contracts that are cancellable or with remaining terms of 12 months or less are not included.</p>

<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the year ended December 31, 2017, we did not have any relationships with unconsolidated organizations or financial partnerships, such as structured finance or special purpose entities that would have been established for the purpose of facilitating off-balance sheet arrangements.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Emerging Growth Company Status</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As an &#8220;emerging growth company,&#8221; or EGC, the Jump-start Our Business Start-ups Act, or JOBS Act, allows us to delay adoption of new or revised accounting pronouncements applicable to public companies until such pronouncements are made applicable to private companies. We have elected to use this extended transition period under the JOBS Act. As a result, our financial statements may not be comparable to the financial statements of issuers who are required to comply with the effective dates for new or revised accounting standards that are applicable to public companies, which may make our common stock less attractive to investors.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>discussion<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and analysis<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>our financial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>condition<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and results of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>operations are based upon our financial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>statements<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>have been prepared in accordance with GAAP. The preparation of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>these financial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>statements<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>requires us to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>make estimates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and judgments that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>affect<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the reported<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>amounts of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>assets and liabilities<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>and related<font style="color:#000000;"> </font>disclosure<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>contingent assets and liabilities,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>revenue and expenses<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>at<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the date of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the financial statements.<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>Generally, we base our estimates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>on historical<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>experience<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and on various other assumptions in accordance with GAAP that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>we believe<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>be reasonable<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>under the circumstances. Actual results may<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>differ<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>these estimates.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Critical<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>accounting<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>policies<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and estimates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are those that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>we consider the most<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>important<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the portrayal of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>our financial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>condition<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and results of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>operations because<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>they require our most<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>difficult, subjective<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>complex judgments, often<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>as a result of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the need to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>make estimates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>about the effect<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of matters<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are inherently<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>uncertain. <p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;letter-spacing:-0.2pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Signed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>agreements<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>are<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>used<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>as<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>evidence<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>an<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>arrangement.<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>If<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>a<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>signed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>contract<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>by<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>the<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>customer does<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>not<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>exist,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>we<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>have<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>historically<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>used<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>either<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>a<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>purchase<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>order<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>a<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>signed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>order<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>form<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>as<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>evidence<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>an arrangement.<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>In<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>cases<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>where<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>both<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>a<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>signed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>contract<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>and<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>either<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>a<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>purchase<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>order<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>signed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>order<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>form<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>exist, we<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>consider<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>the<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>signed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>contract<font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>be<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>the<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>final<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>persuasive<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>evidence<font style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </font>of<font <p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>revenue is recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>ratably over the contract<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>term<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>beginning<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>on the commencement<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>date of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>each subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>term,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>is generally<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the date we make the subscribed applications<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>available<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>customers.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Once the subscribed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>application<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>is available<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>customers, amounts that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>we have the contractual right to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>invoice<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>are recorded in accounts receivable<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and in deferred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>revenue. Professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services are priced either on a fixed-fee or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a time-and-materials<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>basis. Professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services revenue is recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as the services are delivered.<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>In<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>instances where final acceptance of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>non-standard service deliverables<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>are required before revenue is recognized, revenue and the associated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are deferred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>until all<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>acceptance criteria have been met.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We assess collectability<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>based on a number of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>factors<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>such as past collection<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>history with the customer<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and creditworthiness of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the customer.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>If<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>we determine collectability<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>is not reasonably assured, we defer<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the revenue recognition<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>until collectability<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>becomes reasonably<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>assured. We assess whether the fee is fixed or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>determinable<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>based on the payment terms<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>associated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>with the transaction and whether the sales price is subject to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>refund or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>adjustment.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Our<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>arrangements<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>do not include general<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>rights of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>return.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We derive revenue from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>two sources:<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>(1)<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>subscription<font </font>the standard support that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>is included<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the basic subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>we refer<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>as premium<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>support offerings,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and fees for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>subscription<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services, which consist of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>fees associated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>with the implementation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and configuration<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>our applications,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as well<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as<font style="color:#000000;"> </font>fees for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in-person training and TBM Council<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>conference registration and sponsorship<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees. Implementation and configuration<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services primarily consist of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>consultative<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services, such as data mapping<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and establishing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>best practices.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Implementation and configuration<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services do not result in any significant<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>customization or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>modification<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the software<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>platform<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>user interface.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>We present revenue from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>each of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>these sources separately in our consolidated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>financial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>statements.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We enter<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>into arrangements<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>with multiple<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>deliverables<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>primarily include<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services, but may<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>also include<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>premium<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>support,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>online<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>training and in-person training.<font style="color:#000000;"> </font>The professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services are not considered<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>essential<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the functionality<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the software.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>To qualify<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as a separate unit of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>accounting, the delivered<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>item<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>must<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>have value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the customer<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>on a stand-alone basis. We believe<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>offerings and professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>service offerings have stand-alone<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>value. Subscriptions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>have stand-alone<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>because<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>such services are often<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>sold separately from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>other professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services. Professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services have stand-alone<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>because<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>those services may<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>be sold separately by other<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>vendors and there<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are trained third-party<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>consultants capable<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>performing<font style="color:#000000;"> </font>the professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services. Deliverables<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are accounted for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>separately consist of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>software subscription, professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services, premium<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>support and online or in-person<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>training.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">When arrangements<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>involve<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>multiple<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>elements that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>qualify<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as separate units of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>accounting, we allocate<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>revenue to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>each deliverable<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>in a multiple-deliverable<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>arrangement<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>based upon its relative selling<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>price. The estimated selling<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>price for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>each element is based upon the following<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>hierarchy in order<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>priority:<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>vender specific objective<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>evidence,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>VSOE, of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>selling<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>price, if available,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>third-party evidence,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>TPE, of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>selling<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>price, if VSOE of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>selling<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>price is not available,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>best estimate<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>selling price, or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>BESP,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>if neither VSOE of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>selling<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>price, nor TPE<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>selling<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>price is available.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU60"></a>We determine VSOE of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>selling<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>price based on historical<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>stand-alone<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>sales to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>customers.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>In determining VSOE, we require that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a substantial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>majority of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the selling<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>prices for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>our subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>or professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services fall within<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>a reasonably<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>narrow pricing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>range of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the applicable<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>median selling price. We have not yet<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>been able<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>establish<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>VSOE for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>our subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services because<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>we have not historically<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>priced our service offerings within<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>a sufficiently narrow range. When VSOE cannot be established,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>we apply<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>judgment with respect<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>whether we can establish<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>a selling price based on TPE. TPE<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>is determined based on third-party<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>prices for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>similar </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">59</p>

</font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">from</font><font <p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We estimate<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>BESP<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>subscriptions, premium<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>support and online<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>training based on the historical<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>amounts for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>such deliverables<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>on a stand-alone<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>basis. The BESP<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services is based on the historical<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>average rate<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>per hour charged, and BESP<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in-person training is based on historical<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>amounts on a per-seat<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>basis.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We recognize<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>revenue for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees from<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>are typically<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>one-to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>three<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;">-</font>years.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Our<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>arrangements generally<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>do not allow<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the customer<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the contractual right to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>take possession<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the software;<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>support offerings and subscription-based online<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>training are generally<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>one-year agreements billed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>upfront,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>ratably over the term<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the support or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>training agreement.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Our<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>premium<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>support offerings include<font </font>support services, with enhanced<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>response times,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>dedicated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>support resources,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>access to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>architecture<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and </font>recorded training sessions.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services revenue consists of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>fees associated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>with application<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>configuration, integration, change<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>management,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>education<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and training services, and conference registration and sponsorship<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services engagements are priced either on a time-and-materials<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>basis or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>on a fixed-fee basis. The duration of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>our professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services engagements varies based on the scope of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>services requested, but typically<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>ranges between<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>three<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and six months.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>For time-and-materials arrangements,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>we recognize<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>revenue as hours are worked.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>For fixed-fee arrangements,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>we recognize<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services revenue as delivered<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>using<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the percentage of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>completion, or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>POC method,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>measured on an hours incurred basis. Under the POC method of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>accounting, revenue and expenses<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as work is performed<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>based on the relationship<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>between<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>actual hours incurred and total estimated hours at<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the completion<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the project.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Changes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the original<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>estimates may<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>be required during the life of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the project.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Estimates of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>both hours and costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>complete a project are reviewed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>periodically<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>and the effect<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>any change<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the estimated hours to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>complete a project is reflected as an adjustment to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>revenue in the period the change<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>becomes known.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the event current<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>estimated costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>complete a project exceed the revenue allocated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the project,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a loss equal<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the amount of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>estimated excess costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>will<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>be recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the period the change<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>becomes known. The use of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the POC method of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>accounting<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>involves<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>considerable<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>use of estimates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in determining revenue, costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and profits<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and in assigning<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the amounts to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>accounting periods. Associated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>out-of-pocket<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>travel expenses<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>related to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the delivery<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services are typically<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>reimbursed by the customer.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Out-of-pocket<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>reimbursements<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as revenue and cost<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>service expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as incurred.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fees for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in-person training are billed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in advance<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the training and are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the period the training occurs.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Conference registration and sponsorship<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees are for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>TBM Council conferences and related TBM Council<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>activities. Registration<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>TBM Council<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>conferences are billed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in advance<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the conference and are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the period the conference occurs.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>TBM Council<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>sponsorship<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees are billed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in advance<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the period the sponsorship activities occur,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>ratably over the contractual period if the sponsorship<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>entails<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>ongoing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>activities beyond<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>a single<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>event.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>occasion, we sell<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>subscriptions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>through third-party<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>resellers. These arrangements<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>typically call<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the reseller to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>retain a portion of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the price to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the customer<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>as compensation. Since<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>we are typically<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>responsible<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the acceptability<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the services purchased by the customer,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>we are the<font style="color:#000000;"> </font>primary<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>obligor<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the transaction and, therefore,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>record<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>revenue on a gross-basis based on the amount billed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the customer.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Reseller<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as sales and marketing expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as incurred.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred revenue represents<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the unearned<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>revenue on cash receipts or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>accounts receivable for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the sale of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>subscriptions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services have not yet<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>been provided. The substantial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>majority of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>deferred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>revenue relates to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>revenue.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU61"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stock-based</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Compensation</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We measure and recognize<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>compensation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>all<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>stock-based awards granted to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>our employees<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and other<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>service providers, based on the estimated fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the award on the date of grant,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>is recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>on a straight-line basis over the vesting period of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the award based on the estimated portion of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the award that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>is expected to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>vest.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We use the Black-Scholes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>option pricing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>model to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>measure the fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>stock-based awards, other than restricted stock units, or RSUs, when<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>they are granted.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> RSUs are valued based on the market closing price for our Class A common stock as reported on the Nasdaq Global Market on the date of grant. </font>We make several estimates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in determining stock-based compensation and these estimates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>generally<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>require significant<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>analysis<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and judgment to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>develop.<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>These assumptions and estimates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are as follows:</p>

<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#231F20;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;">Fair Value</font><font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;font-family:Times New Roman;"> </font><font style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;">of</font><font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.05pt;font-family:Times New Roman;"> </font><font style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;">Common Stock</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">. Prior to our IPO in September 2016, our board of directors considered numerous objective and subjective factors to determine the fair value of our common stock at each grant date. These factors included, but were not limited to, (i) contemporaneous valuations performed by unrelated third-party valuation firms, (ii) the prices, rights, preferences and privileges of our preferred stock relative to those of our common stock, (iii) the lack of marketability of our common stock, (iv) our stage of development; and (v) the likelihood of achieving a liquidity event, such as an initial public offering or a merger or acquisition of our business given prevailing market conditions.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:10.47%;text-indent:0%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Subsequent to the completion of our IPO we use the market-closing price for our Class A common stock as reported on the Nasdaq Global Market.</p>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>addition<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the assumptions used in the Black-Scholes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>option pricing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>model, we elected to estimate<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a forfeiture<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>rate<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>calculate<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the stock-based compensation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>awards. Our<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>forfeiture rate<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>is derived from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>historical<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>employee<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>termination behavior. If<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the actual number of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>forfeitures<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>differs from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>these estimates,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>additional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>adjustments to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>compensation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>will<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>be required.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Income Taxes</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our provision for income taxes, deferred tax assets and liabilities, and reserves for unrecognized tax benefits reflect our best assessment of estimated future taxes to be paid. Significant judgments and estimates based on interpretations of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>existing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>laws<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>regulations<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the U.S. and the numerous foreign jurisdictions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>where we are subject to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>income tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are required in determining our<font style="color:#000000;"> </font>provision<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>income taxes.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Changes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>laws, statutory<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>rates,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and estimates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>our future<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>taxable income could<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>impact the deferred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>assets and liabilities<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>provided<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in the consolidated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>financial statements<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and would<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>require an adjustment to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the provision<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>income taxes.</p>

style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">include</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the cumul</font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ative pre-tax</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">book income for</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the past three</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">years, scheduled</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">reversals of</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">deferred</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant:
