Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">liabilities,</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">our history of</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">earnings</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">and reliable</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">forecasting, projections</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">of</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">pre-tax</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">book income over the foreseeable</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">future,</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">and the impact of</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">any feasible</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">and </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">prudent tax</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">planning</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">strategies.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We recognize<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the impact of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>position<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in our consolidated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>financial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>statements<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>only if that position<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>is more<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>likely<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>than not of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>being<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>sustained<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>upon examination<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>by taxing authorities, based on the technical<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>merits<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the position. Tax authorities may<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>examine our returns<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in the jurisdictions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>we do business<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and we regularly assess the tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>risk of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>our return<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>filing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>positions. Due to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the complexity of some of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the uncertainties, the ultimate resolution<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>may<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>result in payments that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are materially different from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>our current<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>estimate<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>liability.<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>These differences,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>as well<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as any interest<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and penalties, will<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>be reflected in the provision<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>income taxes in the period in which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>they are determined.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capitalized<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Internal<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Use Software</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We capitalize certain costs incurred for the development of computer software for internal use. These costs generally relate to the development of our technology platform and applications. We capitalize these costs during the development of the project, when it is determined that it is probable that the project will be completed, and the software will be used as intended. Costs related to preliminary project activities, post-implementation activities, training and maintenance are expensed as incurred. Internal-use software is amortized on a straight-line basis over our estimated useful life, generally three years, and the amortization expense is recorded as a component of cost of subscriptions for projects associated with delivery of our technology platform and applications, or through operating expenses for projects associated with internal operations. Management evaluates the useful lives of these assets on an annual basis and tests for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances occur that could impact the recoverability of these assets.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recently Adopted<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>Accounting<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>Pronouncements</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In May 2017, the Financial Accounting Standards Board, or FASB, issued Accounting Standards Update, or ASU, 2017-09 <font style="font-style:italic;">Compensation-Stock Compensation (Topic 718) Scope of Modification Accounting.</font> ASU 2017-09 provides clarification on when modification accounting should be used for changes to the terms or conditions of a share-based payment award. This ASU does not change the accounting for modifications but clarifies that modification accounting guidance should only be applied if there is a change to the value, vesting conditions, or award classification and would not be required if the changes are considered non-substantive. We elected to early adopt this new standard in the second quarter of 2017. <font style="color:#231F20;">The adoption</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">of</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">this standard did not</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">have a material impact on our financial</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In March 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-09, <font style="font-style:italic;">Stock Compensation (Topic 718): Improvements to Employee Share-Based Payment Accounting,</font> which simplifies several aspects of the accounting for employee share-based payment transactions, including the accounting for income taxes, forfeitures, and statutory tax withholding requirements, as well as classification in the statement of cash flows. For public entities, ASU 2016-09 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2016, including interim periods within those fiscal years. We <font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;">adopted this new standard as of January 1, 2017. As of December 31, 2016, we had accumulated excess tax benefits from temporary differences resulting from the amount and timing of stock-based compensation expense recorded in our financial statements compared to deductions on our income tax return from the award compensation that reduces the net operating loss deferred tax asset. We provided a full valuation allowance against our net deferred tax assets since it has been determined that it is more likely than not that all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized. Upon adoption of this standard, the stock-based compensation excess tax benefit was eliminated, resulting in an increase to the net operating loss deferred tax asset, with a corresponding increase in the valuation allowance. We elected to continue to estimate the number of share-based awards expected to vest, rather than electing to account for forfeitures as they occur to determine the amount of stock-based compensation expense to be recognized each period. </font><font style="color:#231F20;">The adoption</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">of</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">this standard did not</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">have a material impact on our financial</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">statements.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">62</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU63"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">New Accounting</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Pronouncements</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Not Yet Adopted</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In October 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-16<font style="font-style:italic;">, Inter-Entity Transfers of Assets other than Inventory</font>. The guidance requires entities to recognize the income tax impact of an intra-entity sale or transfer of an asset other than inventory when the sale or transfer occurs, rather than when the asset has been sold to an outside party.&#160;The guidance will require a modified retrospective application with a cumulative catch-up adjustment to opening retained earnings at the beginning of the first quarter of fiscal 2019, but permits adoption in an earlier period. We are currently evaluating the impact this guidance will have on our consolidated financial statements and the timing of adoption.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In February 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-02, <font style="font-style:italic;">Leases (Topic 842)</font>. The objective of the update is to improve financial reporting by increasing transparency and comparability among organizations by recognizing lease assets and lease liabilities on the balance sheet and disclosing key information about leasing arrangements. For public entities, the new standard is effective for interim and annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2018. For all other entities, the new standard is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2019, and for interim periods within those annual periods beginning after December 15, 2020. Early application of the amendments is permitted for all entities. We are currently evaluating the impact this guidance will have on our financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In May 2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-09, <font style="font-style:italic;">Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606),</font> outlining a single comprehensive model for entities to use in accounting for revenue arising from contracts with customers that supersedes most current revenue recognition guidance with a comprehensive revenue measurement and recognition standard and expanded disclosure requirements. The standard also provides guidance on the recognition of costs related to obtaining customer contracts. For public entities, ASU 2014-09, as amended, is effective for annual periods and interim periods within those annual periods, beginning after December 15, 2017. For all other entities, the new standard is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2018, and interim periods within those annual periods beginning after December 15, 2019, <font style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">and the guidance must be applied retrospectively to each prior period presented or retrospectively with the cumulative effect recognized as of the date of adoption.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are in the process of finalizing our assessment of the new standard, including ascribing the appropriate amortization period to the respective commission costs. We adopted the requirements of the new standard on January 1, 2018 and will utilize the full retrospective transition method. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The impact of adopting this standard on 2017 and 2016 subscription and services revenue is not material. The primary impact of the standard will be the requirement to capitalize certain contract costs, such as commissions, which are currently being expensed as incurred. Because these costs will now be capitalized and amortized over the period benefited by the transaction, we expect that adoption of this standard will result in marginally lower sales and marketing expense in scenarios where current period sales results are higher than the prior period sales results. In scenarios where current period sales results are lower than the prior period sales results, we expect sales and marketing expenses will be marginally higher than if we had expensed these selling costs as incurred. Under the new standard, we will defer commission costs to obtain customer subscription contracts and will amortize these costs over a period of benefit that we have determined to be four years for new subscriptions, and over the term of the respective subscription for renewals of subscription agreements. Commissions on service arrangements will continue to be expensed as incurred as the term for these arrangements is typically less than 12 months. We expect this to materially reduce annual sales and marketing expenses. </p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="ITEM_7A_QUANTITATIVE_QUALITATIVE_DISCLOS"></a><a name="ITEM_7A_QUANTITATIVE_QUALITATIVE_DISCLOS"></a>Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;font-size:6pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Foreign Currency<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>Exchange<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>Risk</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU64"></a>Due to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>our international<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>operations, we have foreign currency<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>risks related to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>revenue and operating expenses<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>denominated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in currencies other<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>than the U.S. dollar, primarily the British<font style="color:#000000;"> </font>Pound<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>Sterling, Euro and Australian<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>dollar. Our<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>sales contracts<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are primarily denominated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the local currency<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the customer<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>making the purchase. In<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>addition,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>a portion of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>operating expenses<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>are incurred outside the United<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>States and are denominated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in foreign currencies. Additionally, subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees are largely<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>based on customers&#8217;<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>anticipated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>spend as expressed in U.S. dollars<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as managed by our system,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fee construct<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>may<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>increase the exposure of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>revenue to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>currency<font style="color:#000000;"> </font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">63</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">fluctuations. Decreases in the relative value</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">of</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the U.S. dollar</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">to</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">other</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">currencies may</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">negatively</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">affect revenue and other</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">operating results as expressed in U.S. dollars. We do not believe</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">that</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">an immediate</font><font style="color:#000000;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">10% in</font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">crease or</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">decrease in the relative value</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">of</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the U.S. dollar</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">to</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">other</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">currencies would</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">have a material effect</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">on operating results.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have experienced<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and will<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>continue<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>experience<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fluctuations in net loss as a result of transaction gains<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>losses related to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>remeasuring certain current<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>asset and current<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>liability<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>balances that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are denominated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in currencies other<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>than the functional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>currency<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the entities in which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>they are recorded.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>We have not engaged<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the hedging<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>foreign currency<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>transactions to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>date.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>We are evaluating<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and benefits of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>initiating<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>such a program<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and may<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in the future<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>hedge<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>selected significant<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>transactions denominated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in currencies other<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>than the U.S. dollar<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as we expand international<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>operations.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Rate Sensitivity</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We hold<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>cash and cash equivalents<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>working<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>capital<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>purposes. We do not have material exposure to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>market<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>risk with respect<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>investments,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>as any investments we enter<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>into are primarily highly<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>liquid<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>investments.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font></p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU66"></a><a name="REPORT_INDEPENDENT_REGISTERED_PUBLIC_ACC"></a><font style="color:#auto;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="REPORT_INDEPENDENT_REGISTERED_PUBLIC_ACC"></a>Report of Independent Regist</font><font style="color:#auto;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ered Public Accounting Firm</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">To<font style="font-weight:bold;color:#FF0000;"> </font>the<font style="font-weight:bold;color:#FF0000;"> </font>Board of Directors and Stockholders of </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Apptio, Inc.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Opinion on the Financial Statements</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Apptio, Inc. and its subsidiaries as of December 31, 2017 and 2016, and the related consolidated statements of operations, of comprehensive loss, of changes in convertible preferred stock and stockholders&#8217; equity (deficit) and of cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2017, including the related notes (collectively referred to as the &#8220;consolidated financial statements&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December 31, 2017 and 2016, and the results of their operations and their cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2017 in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basis for Opinion</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">These consolidated financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#8217;s management.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements based on our audits.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (&#8220;PCAOB&#8221;) and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We conducted our audits of these consolidated financial statements in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB.&nbsp;&nbsp;Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. As part of our audits we are required to obtain an understanding of internal control over financial reporting but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company's internal control over financial reporting.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, we express no such opinion.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the consolidated financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the consolidated financial statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the consolidated financial statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">71</p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU72"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Apptio, Inc.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="NOTES_TO_CONSOLIDATED_FINANCIAL_STATEMEN"></a><a name="NOTES_TO_CONSOLIDATED_FINANCIAL_STATEMEN"></a>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="NOTES_TO_UNAUDITED_CONDENSED_CONSOLIDATE"></a>Note 1. Description of Operations and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Operations</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Apptio, Inc. or the Company, was incorporated on October 2, 2007 and is headquartered in Bellevue, Washington. The Company develops and sells Technology Business Management, or TBM, solutions. The Company&#8217;s cloud-based platform and SaaS applications enable IT leaders to analyze, optimize and plan technology investments, and benchmark their financial and operational performance against peers. The Company operates in the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Denmark, the Netherlands, Australia, Canada, France, Singapore and Italy.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Initial Public Offering </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In September&#160;2016, the Company completed an initial public offering, or IPO, in which the Company sold 6,900,000 shares of its newly-authorized Class&#160;A common stock&#160;at the initial price to public of $16.00 per share. The Company received net proceeds of $99.0 million, after deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and offering expenses, from sales of its shares in the IPO.&#160;Immediately prior to the completion of the IPO, (1) all shares of common stock then outstanding were converted to Class&#160;B common stock on a one-for-one basis, (2) common stock warrants then outstanding were converted to warrants to purchase 47,893 shares of Class B common stock on a one-for-one basis, (3) a warrant to purchase 27,321 shares of convertible preferred stock was converted to a warrant to purchase 27,321 shares of Class B common stock, and (4) all shares of convertible preferred stock then outstanding were converted into&#160;18,239,475 shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock on a one-for-one basis, and then reclassified as shares of Class&#160;B common stock. See Note 6 for further discussion of Class&#160;A and B common stock.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred Offering Costs</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred offering costs of $3.7 million, consisting of legal, accounting and other costs related to the IPO, were reclassified to additional paid-in capital as a reduction of the proceeds upon the closing of our IPO on September 28, 2016.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Principles of Consolidation</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The consolidated financial statements include the Company and its wholly-owned subsidiaries. All significant intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Accounting Principles</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes were prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America, or GAAP.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Use of Estimates</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of revenue and expenses during the reporting period. Actual results could differ materially from those estimates.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certain Significant Risks and Uncertainties</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU73"></a>The Company continues to be subject to the risks and challenges associated with other companies at a similar stage of development, including risks associated with: dependence on key personnel; successful marketing and sale of its solutions and adaptation of such solutions to changing market dynamics and customer preferences; </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">72</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Apptio, Inc.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">competition from alternative products and serv</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ices, including from larger companies that have greater name recognition, longer operating histories, more and better established customer relationships and greater resources than the Company; and the ability to raise additional capital to support future g</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">rowth. Since inception through December&#160;31, 2017, the Company has incurred losses from operations, and accumulated a deficit of $225.9 million, and has been dependent on equity and debt financing to fund operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Operating<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Segments</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company follows<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the authoritative literature that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>establishes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>annual<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and interim reporting standards for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>an enterprise&#8217;s operating segments and related disclosures<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>about its products and services, geographic<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>regions and major customers.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company operates its business<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as one operating segment.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Its<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>chief operating decision makers,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>CODMs,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are its Chief Executive<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>Officer<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and Chief Financial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>Officer.<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>The CODMs review separate revenue information for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services revenue, and all<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>other<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>financial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>information presented on a consolidated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>basis, for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>purposes of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>making operating decisions,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>assessing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>financial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>performance<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and allocating<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>resources.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Foreign Currency</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The functional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>currency<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>international<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>subsidiaries<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>is the U.S. dollar. The results of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>operations for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>international<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>subsidiaries<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>are remeasured from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the local currency<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>into U.S. dollars<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>using<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>average exchange<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>rates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>during each period. The majority of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>assets and liabilities<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>are remeasured using<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>exchange<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>rates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>at<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the end of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>each period. All<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>equity transactions and certain assets are remeasured using<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>historical<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>rates.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Comprehensive<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>Loss</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certain gains<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and losses are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in comprehensive<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>loss, but excluded<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>net loss. Comprehensive<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>loss includes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>net loss and unrealized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>gains<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and losses on available-for-sale<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>securities.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and Cash<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>Equivalents</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company considers all<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>highly<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>liquid<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>investments,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>including<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>money market<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>investments with an original<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>maturity<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>three<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>months<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>less at<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the date of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>purchase, to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>be cash equivalents.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Investments</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company classifies<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>its investment securities as available-for-sale.<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>Investment<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>securities are stated<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>at<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>with any unrealized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>gains<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>losses included<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as a component of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>accumulated other<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>comprehensive<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>income (loss)<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in stockholders&#8217;<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> equity (</font>deficit). Realized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>gains<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and losses and declines<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>securities judged<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>be other<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>than temporary<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are included<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in interest<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>income (expense) and other,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>net.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>The cost<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>investments for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>purposes of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>computing realized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and unrealized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>gains<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and losses is based on the specific identification<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>method.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Investments<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in securities with maturities<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>less than one year,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>where management&#8217;s intent is to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>use the investments to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>fund current<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>operations, are classified as short-term<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>investments.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Investments<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>with maturities<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>greater<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>than one year are classified<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as long-term<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>investments.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Value of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Financial Instruments</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December&#160;31, 2017 and 2016 the Company has the following<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>financial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>instruments:<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>cash equivalents,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>marketable securities, accounts receivable,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>accounts payable<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and accrued liabilities.<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU74"></a>The fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>accounts receivable,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>accounts payable,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and certain accrued liabilities<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>approximates their respective carrying amounts.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>The Company measures its cash equivalents,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>marketable securities, </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">73</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Apptio, Inc.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

</font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the fair</font><font that</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">value</font><font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">be based on the assumptions that market</font><font </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">an asset or</font><font <p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>principles<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>require disclosures<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>regarding the manner in which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>is determined for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>assets and liabilities<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>and establishes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>a three-tiered<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>hierarchy into which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>these assets and liabilities<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>must<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>be grouped, based upon significant<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>levels<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>inputs as follows:</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level</font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;letter-spacing:-0.35pt;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">3</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;color:#231F20;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><font style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"></font>Unobservable<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>inputs that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are supported by little or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>no market<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>activity and that are significant<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the assets or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>liabilities.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The lowest level<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>significant<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>input determines the placement of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the entire fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value measurement<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in the hierarchy. Management&#8217;s assessment of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the significance<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a particular input to the fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>measurement<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in its entirety<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>requires management to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>make judgments and consider factors<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>specific to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the asset or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>liability.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Allowance for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Doubtful Accounts</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company performs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>initial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and ongoing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>evaluations<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>its customers&#8217;<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>financial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>positions, and generally<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>extends credit on account, without collateral. The Company determines the need for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>an allowance<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>doubtful accounts based upon various factors,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>including<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>past collection<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>experience, credit quality<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the customer,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>age of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the receivable<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>balance,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and current<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>economic conditions.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">If<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the financial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>condition<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>customers<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>were to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>deteriorate,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>resulting in an impairment of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>their ability<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>make payments,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>additional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>allowances<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>might be required. Accounts are charged against the allowance<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>doubtful accounts once collection<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>efforts<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>are unsuccessful.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Activity within<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the allowance<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>doubtful accounts was as follows (in thousands):</p>

<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Preferred Stock Warrant<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Liability</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company classified<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>its warrants<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>purchase preferred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>stock<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>as a liability.<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>The Company adjusted the carrying value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the warrant<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>liability<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>at<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the end of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>each reporting period utilizing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the Black-Scholes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>option pricing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>model. The preferred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>stock<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>warrant<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>liability<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>was included<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>on the Company&#8217;s consolidated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>balance<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>sheets and its warrant<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>revaluation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>was recorded as interest<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and is included in interest<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>income (expense)<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and other,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>net. <font style="color:#000000;">Immediately prior to the completion of the IPO, the warrant to purchase shares of convertible preferred stock was converted to a warrant to purchase shares of Class B common stock and was no longer classified as a liability on the Company&#8217;s consolidated balance sheets. On September 26, 2016, the warrant holder exercised the warrant and the Company issued shares of Class B common stock through a cashless exercise of the warrant, in accordance with its terms. See Note 5 for additional information.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Revenue<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>Recognition</p>

normal;">The Company derives its revenue from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>two sources:<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>(1)<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>revenue, which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>is comprised of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> associated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>with the implementation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and configuration<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of the </font>fees.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Implementation and configuration<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services primarily consist of consultative<font If<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>collection<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>is </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">75</p>

</font>customers<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>via access to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>recorded training sessions.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU77"></a>Professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services revenue consists of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>fees associated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>with application<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>configuration, integration, change<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>management,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>education<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and training services, and conference registration and sponsorship<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>The Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services engagements are priced either on a time<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;">-</font>and-materials basis or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>on a fixed-fee basis. The duration of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services engagements varies based on the scope of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>services requested, but typically<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>ranges between<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>three<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and six months.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>For time-and-materials<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>arrangements,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company recognizes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>revenue as hours are worked.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>For fixed-fee arrangements,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company recognizes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services revenue as delivered<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>using<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the percentage of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>completion, or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>POC, method measured on an hours incurred basis. Under the POC </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">76</p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</p>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">method of</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">accounting, revenue and </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">be required during the life of</font><font
