<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">If<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>current<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>estimated costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>complete a project exceed the revenue allocated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the project,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a loss equal<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the amount of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>estimated excess costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>will<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>be recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the period the change becomes known. The use of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the POC method of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>accounting<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>involves<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>considerable<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>use of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>estimates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in determining revenue, costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and profits,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and in assigning<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the amounts to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>accounting<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>periods. Associated out-of-pocket<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>travel expenses<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>related to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the delivery<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services are typically<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>reimbursed<font style="color:#000000;"> </font>by the customer.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Out-of-pocket<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>reimbursements<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as revenue and cost<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of service expense.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fees for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in-person training are billed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in advance<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the training and are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the period the training occurs.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Conference registration and sponsorship<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees are for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>TBM Council conferences and related TBM Council<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>activities. Registration<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>TBM Council<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>conferences are billed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in advance<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the conference and are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the period the conference occurs.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>TBM Council<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>sponsorship<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees are paid<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in advance<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the period the sponsorship activities occur,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>ratably over the contractual period if the sponsorship<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>entails<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>ongoing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>activities beyond<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>a single<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>event.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>occasion, the Company sells<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>its subscriptions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>through third-party<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>resellers. These arrangements<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>typically<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>call<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the reseller to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>retain a portion of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the price to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the customer<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>as compensation. Since<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the Company is typically<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>responsible<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the acceptability<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the services purchased by the customer,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company is the primary<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>obligor<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the transaction and, therefore, records<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>revenue on a gross basis based on the amount billed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the customer.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Reseller<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>fees are recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as sales and marketing expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as incurred.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred revenue represents<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the unearned<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>revenue on cash receipts or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>accounts receivable for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the sale of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>subscriptions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>professional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services have not yet<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>been provided. The substantial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>majority of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>deferred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>revenue relates to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>subscription<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>revenue.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Research<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and Development</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Research and development<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are expensed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as incurred and primarily include<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>payroll, employee<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>benefits, consulting<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>services, stock-based compensation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and other<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>headcount-related costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>associated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>with product development<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and depreciation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>equipment used in research and development.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capitalized<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Software<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Costs</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For development<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>related to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>software<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>solutions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and internal use software, qualifying<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>internally<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>developed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>software<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>costs,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>including<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>payroll<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and stock-based compensation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>costs, incurred during the application<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>development<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>stage are capitalized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and recorded in property<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and equipment, net.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Costs related to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>preliminary project activities and post-implementation activities are expensed<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>as incurred. The Company capitalized $0.7 million, $1.1 million and $0.8 million<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>software<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>development<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>during the years ended<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>December 31, 2017, 2016 and<font style="color:#000000;"> 2015, </font>respectively. Stock-based compensation costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>included<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in capitalized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>software<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>costs and amortization of capitalized software costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>were immaterial to the consolidated financial statements for all years presented.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font></p>

<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company allocates<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>certain overhead and information technology<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>operating costs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>between cost<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>goods sold, research and development, sales and marketing,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and general<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and administration expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>based upon the number of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>employees<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in the related departments.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU78"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Sales Commissions</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company pays sales commissions to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>employees<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>shortly after<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>executing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>customer agreements related to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>initial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>sales and subsequent<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>renewals<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>all<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>subscriptions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and related services. Sales<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>commission obligations<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>are accrued to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>sales and marketing at<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the time<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the initial<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>sale for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the full amount of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the contract.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Income Taxes</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company follows<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the asset and liability<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>method of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>accounting<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>income taxes.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>This method requires recognition<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>deferred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>assets and liabilities<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the expected future<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>tax consequences<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>temporary<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>differences between<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the carrying amounts and the tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>basis of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>assets and liabilities.<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>A valuation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>allowance<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>has been established<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the full amount of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the net deferred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>assets as the Company has determined that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the future<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>realization<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>benefit is not more<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>likely<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>than not.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company recognizes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>benefit from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>uncertain tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>positions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>only if it is more<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>likely than not that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>position<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>will<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>be sustained<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>on examination<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>by the tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>authorities, based on the technical<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>merits<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the position. The tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>benefit is measured based on the largest benefit that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>is more likely<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>than not of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>being<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>realized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>upon ultimate settlement.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>The Company recognizes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>interest<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and penalties<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>on amounts due to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>taxing authorities as a component of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>income tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>expense.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>annual<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>effective<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>rate is based on expected income, statutory<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>rates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>planning<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>opportunities<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>available<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>in the various jurisdictions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the Company operates.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Significant<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>judgment is required in determining the Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>annual<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>effective<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>rate<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and in evaluating<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>positions.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stock-Based<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>Compensation</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company recognizes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>related to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>stock-based compensation. Compensation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>cost<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for the years ended December 31,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>2017, 2016 and 2015 includes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>costs for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>all<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>share-based compensation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>arrangements<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>based on the grant-date<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value and is recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>using<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>the straight-line attribution method.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>stock<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>price volatility<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and expected option life involve<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>management&#8217;s best estimates,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>both of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>which<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>impact the fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the award calculated<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>under the Black-Scholes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>option pricing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>model and, ultimately, the expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>will<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>be recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>over the life of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the award. The Company has elected to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>recognize<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>compensation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>only the portion of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>awards expected to vest.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Therefore,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>management appli<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">e</font>s an estimated forfeiture<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>rate<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>is derived from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>historical employee<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>termination behavior. If<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the actual number of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>forfeitures<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>differs<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>these estimates, additional<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>adjustments to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>compensation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>expense<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>may<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>be required.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="T1"></a><a name="T3"></a>In May 2017, the Financial Accounting Standards Board, or <a name="T1"></a>FASB, issued Accounting Standards Update, or ASU, 2017-09 <font style="font-style:italic;">Compensation-Stock Compensation (Topic 718) Scope of Modification Accounting.</font><a name="T3"></a> ASU 2017-09 provides clarification on when modification accounting should be used for changes to the terms or conditions of a share-based payment award. This ASU does not change the accounting for modifications but clarifies that modification accounting guidance should only be applied if there is a change to the value, vesting conditions, or award classification and would not be required if the changes are considered non-substantive. The Company elected to early adopt this new standard in the second quarter of 2017. <font style="color:#231F20;">The adoption</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">of</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">this standard did not</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU79"></a>In March 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-09, <font style="font-style:italic;">Stock Compensation (Topic 718): Improvements to Employee Share-Based Payment Accounting,</font> which simplifies several aspects of the accounting for employee share-based payment transactions, including the accounting for income taxes, forfeitures, and statutory tax withholding requirements, as well as classification in the statement of cash flows. For public entities, ASU 2016-09 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2016, including interim periods within those fiscal years. The Company <font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;">adopted this new standard as of January 1, 2017. As of December 31, 2016, the Company has accumulated excess tax benefits from temporary differences resulting from the amount and timing of stock-based compensation expense recorded in our financial statements compared to deductions on its income tax return from </font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">78</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Apptio, Inc.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;">the award compensation that reduces the net operating loss deferred tax asset. The Company provided a full valuation allowance against its net deferred tax assets since i</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;">t has been determined that it is more likely than not that all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized. Upon adoption of this standard, the stock-based compensation excess tax benefit was eliminated, resulting in an increase to the net operating </font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;">lo</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;">ss deferred tax asset, with a corresponding</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> increase in the</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> valuation allowance</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;">. The Company elected to continue to estimate the number of share-based awards expected to vest, rather than electing to account for forfeitures as they occur to determine the a</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;">mount of stock-based compensation expense to be recognized each period. </font><font style="color:#231F20;">The adoption</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">of</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">this standard did not</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial</font><font style="color:#231F20;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;">statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">New Accounting Pronouncements Not Yet Adopted</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In October 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-16<font style="font-style:italic;">, Inter-Entity Transfers of Assets other than Inventory</font>. The guidance requires entities to recognize the income tax impact of an intra-entity sale or transfer of an asset other than inventory when the sale or transfer occurs, rather than when the asset has been sold to an outside party.&#160;The guidance will require a modified retrospective application with a cumulative catch-up adjustment to opening retained earnings at the beginning of the first quarter of fiscal 2019, but permits adoption in an earlier period. The Company is currently evaluating the impact this guidance will have on our consolidated financial statements and the timing of adoption.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In February 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-02, <font style="font-style:italic;">Leases (Topic 842)</font>. The objective of the update is to improve financial reporting by increasing transparency and comparability among organizations by recognizing lease assets and lease liabilities on the balance sheet and disclosing key information about leasing arrangements. For public entities, the new standard is effective for interim and annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2018. For all other entities, the new standard is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2019, and for interim periods within those annual periods beginning after December 15, 2020. Early application of the amendments is permitted for all entities. The Company is currently evaluating the impact this guidance will have on the Company&#8217;s financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In May 2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-09, <font style="font-style:italic;">Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606),</font> outlining a single comprehensive model for entities to use in accounting for revenue arising from contracts with customers that supersedes most current revenue recognition guidance with a comprehensive revenue measurement and recognition standard and expanded disclosure requirements. The standard also provides guidance on the recognition of costs related to obtaining customer contracts. For public entities, ASU 2014-09, as amended, is effective for annual periods and interim periods within those annual periods, beginning after December 15, 2017. For all other entities, the new standard is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2018, and interim periods within those annual periods beginning after December 15, 2019, <font style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">and the guidance must be applied retrospectively to each prior period presented or retrospectively with the cumulative effect recognized as of the date of adoption.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is in process of finalizing its assessment of the new standard, including ascribing the appropriate amortization period to the respective commission costs. The Company adopted the requirements of the new standard on January 1, 2018 and will utilize the full retrospective transition method. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The impact of adopting this standard on 2017 and 2016 subscription and services revenue is not material. The primary impact of the standard will be the requirement to capitalize certain contract costs, such as commissions, which are currently being expensed as incurred. Because these costs will now be capitalized and amortized over the period benefited by the transaction, the Company expects that adoption of this standard will result in marginally lower sales and marketing expense in scenarios where current period sales results are higher than the prior period sales results. In scenarios where current period sales results are lower than the prior period sales results, the Company expects sales and marketing expenses will be marginally higher than if the Company had expensed these selling costs as incurred. Under the new standard, the Company will defer commission costs to obtain customer subscription contracts and will amortize these costs over a period of benefit that we have determined to be four years for new subscription agreements, and over the term of the respective subscription for renewals of subscription agreements. Commissions on service arrangements will continue to be expensed as incurred as the term for these arrangements is typically less than 12 months. The Company expects this to materially reduce annual sales and marketing expenses. </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">79</p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As interest rates increase, those securities purchased at a lower yield show a mark-to-market unrealized loss. The longer the duration of these securities, the more susceptible they are to changes in market interest rates and bond yields. The unrealized losses are due primarily to changes in interest rates. The Company regularly reviews investments for other-than-temporary impairment using both qualitative and quantitative criteria. </p>

<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 5. Warrants </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Common Stock Warrants</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with entering into and amending the senior credit facility, see Note 12, the Company issued warrants to purchase an aggregate of 21,208 shares of Class B common stock at an exercise price of $14.31 per share. On September 26, 2016, one of the warrant holders exercised warrants to purchase 10,604 shares of Class B common stock. The remaining warrants to purchase 10,604 shares of Class B common stock were outstanding as of December&#160;31, 2017. </p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Convertible Preferred Stock Warrant</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company previously issued a warrant to purchase 27,321 shares of Series A convertible preferred stock in conjunction with a loan and security agreement with Silicon Valley Bank, or SVB, at an exercise price of $1.37255 per share. Immediately prior to the completion of the IPO, this warrant was converted to a warrant to purchase 27,321 shares of Class B common stock. On September 26, 2016, the warrant holder exercised the warrant and the Company issued 25,658 shares of Class B common stock through a cashless exercise of the warrant, in accordance with its terms. </p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 6. Stockholders&#8217; Equity</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Preferred Stock<font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">&#160;</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2017, the Company had authorized 5,000,000 shares of preferred stock, par value $0.0001, of which no shares were issued and outstanding.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Common Stock</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2017 the Company had authorized 451,000,000 shares of Class&#160;A common stock and 44,000,000 shares of Class&#160;B common stock, each par value $0.0001 per share, of which 27,402,965 shares and 14,709,981 shares of Class&#160;A and Class&#160;B common stock, respectively, were issued and outstanding. Holders of Class&#160;A and Class&#160;B common stock are entitled to one vote per share and ten votes per share, respectively. Each share of Class B common stock is convertible at any time at the option of the holder into one share of Class A common stock. In addition, each share of Class B common stock will convert automatically into one share of Class A common stock upon transfer, subject to certain exceptions, and upon the earlier of (1) the seventh anniversary of the closing of the IPO, and (2) the date on which the Class B common stock ceases to represent at least 25% of the outstanding common stock. The shares of Class&#160;A common stock and Class&#160;B common stock are identical, except for voting and conversion rights. During the year ended December&#160;31, 2017, 16,782,886 shares of Class B common stock were converted into 16,782,886 shares of Class A common stock at the request of the holders thereof. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 7. Equity Incentive Plans</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2016 Equity Incentive Plan</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU81"></a>The Company&#8217;s 2016 Equity Incentive Plan, or the 2016 Plan, became effective on&#160;September 21, 2016. The 2016 Plan provides for the grant of incentive stock options, or ISOs, within the meaning of Section 422 of the Internal Revenue Code, to the Company&#8217;s employees or any of the Company&#8217;s subsidiaries&#8217; employees, and for the grant of nonstatutory stock options, or NSOs, restricted stock, restricted stock units, or RSUs, stock appreciation </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">82</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Apptio, Inc.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">rights, performance units and performance shares to employees, directors and consultants of the Company and the Company&#8217;s subsidiaries&#8217; employees and consultants. As of</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> December 31, 2017, the total number of shares available for issuance under the 2016 Plan was 4,237,746. These available shares will automatically increase each January&#160;1, by the least of 5,500,000 shares of Class A common stock, by 5% of the outstanding s</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">hares of all classes of the Company&#8217;s common stock as of the last day of the Company&#8217;s immediately preceding fiscal year, and such other amount as the Company&#8217;s board of directors may determine on or before the last day of the Company&#8217;s immediately precedi</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ng fiscal year. Pursuant to the above, on January 1, 2018, the number of available shares automatically increased by 2,105,647.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2007 Stock Plan</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company granted options under its 2007 stock plan, as amended, or the 2007 Plan, until September 23, 2016, when the plan was terminated in connection with the Company&#8217;s IPO. Accordingly, no shares are available for future issuance under this plan. The 2007 Plan continues to govern outstanding equity awards granted thereunder.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2011 Executive Equity Incentive Plan</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company granted options under its 2011 executive equity incentive plan as amended, or the 2011 Plan, until September 23, 2016, when the plan was terminated in connection with the Company&#8217;s IPO. Accordingly, no shares are available for future issuance under this plan. The 2011 Plan continues to govern outstanding equity awards granted thereunder.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2016 Employee Stock Purchase Plan</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s&#160;Employee Stock Purchase Plan, or 2016 ESPP, became effective on&#160;September 21, 2016. As of December 31, 2017, the total number of shares of Class A common stock available for issuance under the 2016 ESPP was 821,635 These available shares will automatically increase each January&#160;1, by the least of 1,600,000 shares of Class A common stock, 1% of the number of shares of all classes of the Company&#8217;s common stock outstanding on the immediately preceding fiscal year, and such lesser number of shares as determined by the Company&#8217;s board of directors. Pursuant to the above, on January 1, 2018, the number of available shares automatically increased by 421,129.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The 2016&#160;ESPP&#160;allows eligible employees to purchase shares of the Company&#8217;s Class&#160;A common stock at a discount through payroll deductions of their eligible compensation, subject to any plan limitations. Except for the initial offering period, the 2016&#160;ESPP&#160;provides for separate six-month offering periods beginning November&#160;30 and May&#160;31 of each fiscal year. The initial offering period ran from September 23, 2016 through May 31, 2017. The initial offering period included the employee enrollment period, which ran from September 23, 2016 to November 10, 2016, at which time employee deductions commenced.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On each purchase date, eligible employees will purchase the Company&#8217;s Class A common stock at a price per share equal to 85% of the lesser of (1)&#160;the fair market value of the Company&#8217;s Class A common stock on the first trading day of the offering period, and/or (2)&#160;the fair market value of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the purchase date.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stock Options</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stock options are exercisable at a price equal to the market value of the underlying shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the date of the grant as determined by the Company&#8217;s board of directors or, for those stock options issued subsequent to the IPO, the closing price of the Company&#8217;s common stock as reported on the Nasdaq Global Market on the date of grant.<font style="font-family:inherit;"> Stock options granted under the 2016 Plan, 2011 Plan and the 2007 Plan generally vest 25% one year from the date the requisite service period begins and continue to vest monthly for each month of continued employment over the remaining three years. Options granted generally are exercisable for a period of up to 10 years.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">83</p>

<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The weighted-average<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>grant<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>date fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>per share of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>options granted during 2017, 2016 and 2015 was $5.94, $5.73 and $6.05, respectively. The total fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>shares vested during 2017, 2016 and 2015 was $11.6 million,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>$8.3 millio<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">n</font> and $7.6 millio<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">n</font>,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The total intrinsic value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>options exercised during 2017, 2016 and 2015 was $38.5 million,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>$2.9 millio<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">n</font> and $5.4 millio<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">n</font>, respectively. During<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> 2017, </font>2016 and 2015, the Company received $21.9 million, $1.3 millio<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">n and</font> $2.7 millio<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;">n</font>,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>respectively, from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>exercises of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>stock<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>options. Shares are issued<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>plan<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>reserves<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>upon exercise.</p>

<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The weighted-average<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>volatility<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>used in the fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>calculations<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>option grants<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>for 2017,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>2016 and 2015, was 34.7%, 38.9%<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> and </font>42.7%,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has not declared<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>paid<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>any dividends.<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>The risk-free<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>interest<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>rate<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>used in the Black-Scholes<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>option pricing<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>model is based on the implied<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>yield<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>available<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>at<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the time<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the option grant<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in U.S. Treasury securities at<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>maturity<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>with a term<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>equivalent<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the expected life of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the option. Expected volatility<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>is based on an average volatility<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>stock<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>prices for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a group of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>publicly<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>traded companies<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>with similar software<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>product offerings.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>The expected life of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>options represents<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the period that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the stock-based awards are expected to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>be outstanding. Consideration<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>was given<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the contractual terms<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the stock-based awards, vesting schedules<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and expectations of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>future<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>employee behavior. Prior to the IPO, given the absence<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>an active market<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>common<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>stock,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company&#8217;s board of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>directors<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>was required to<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>estimate<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the fair<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>value<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the Company&#8217;s<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>common<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>stock<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>at<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the time of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>each option grant<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>based on several factors,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>including<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>consideration<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>input from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>management and contemporaneous third-party<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>valuations.<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>These valuations<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>include<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>consideration<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>enterprise value and assessment of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>other<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>common<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and convertible<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>preferred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>stock<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>transactions occurring during the period. Subsequent to the completion of the IPO, the Company uses the market-closing price for the Company&#8217;s Class A common stock as reported on the Nasdaq Global Market.</p>

The aggregate grant date fair value of RSUs granted in 2017 and 2016 was $27.8 million and $10.4 million, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:8pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 8. Net Loss Per Share Attributable to Common Stockholders</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company calculates basic and diluted net loss per share attributable to common stockholders in conformity with the two-class method required for companies with participating securities. The Company considers all series of convertible preferred stock to be participating securities. Under the two-class method, the net loss attributable to common stockholders is not allocated to the convertible preferred stock as the holders of convertible preferred stock do not have a contractual obligation to share in losses.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The diluted net loss per share attributable to common stockholders is computed by giving effect to all potential dilutive common stock equivalents outstanding for the period. For purposes of this calculation, convertible preferred stock, options to purchase common stock and warrants to purchase common stock and convertible preferred stock are considered common stock equivalents, but have been excluded from the calculation of diluted net loss per share attributable to common stockholders as their effect is antidilutive. Basic and diluted net loss per share was the same for each period presented, as the inclusion of all potential common shares outstanding would have been antidilutive.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following table sets forth the computation of basic and diluted net loss per share (in thousands, except per share data):</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 9. Income Taxes</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On&#160;December&#160;22, 2017, the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, or the Tax Act, was signed into law making significant changes to the Internal Revenue Code. Changes include, but are not limited to, a federal corporate tax rate decrease from&#160;35%&#160;to&#160;21%&#160;for tax years beginning after&#160;December&#160;31, 2017, the transition of U.S international taxation from a worldwide tax system to a territorial system, and a one-time transition tax on the mandatory deemed repatriation of foreign earnings. The Company has estimated the provision for income taxes in accordance with the Tax Act and guidance available as of the date of this filing, and as a result recorded a reduction of&#160;$30.0 million&#160;in its deferred tax assets, which is entirely offset by its valuation allowance resulting in zero total tax expense in the period in which the legislation was enacted. The provisional amount related to the re-measurement of certain deferred tax assets and liabilities, based on the rates at which they are expected to reverse in the future, was&#160;$30.0 million. The provisional amount related to the one-time transition tax on the mandatory deemed repatriation of foreign earnings was $0.7 million based on cumulative foreign earnings of $5.5 million.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On December 22, 2017, Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 118, or SAB 118, was issued to address the application of GAAP in situations when a registrant does not have the necessary information available, prepared, or analyzed (including computations) in reasonable detail to complete the accounting for certain income tax effects of the Tax Act. Additional work is necessary for a more detailed analysis of the deferred tax assets and liabilities and the Company&#8217;s historical foreign earnings as well as potential correlative adjustments. Any subsequent adjustment to these amounts will be recorded to current tax expense in the quarter of 2018 when the analysis is complete.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The components of loss before provision for income taxes were as follows (in thousands):</p>

ASC<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>740, <font style="font-style:italic;">Income</font><font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="font-style:italic;">Taxe</font><font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">s</font>,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>provides that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>benefit from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>an uncertain tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>position<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>may<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>be recognized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>when<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>it is more<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>likely<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>than not that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the position<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>will be sustained<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>upon examination, including<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>resolutions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>any related appeals<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>or<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>litigation<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>processes, on the basis of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the technical<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>merits.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>The Company has assessed its income tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>positions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and recorded tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>benefits for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>all<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>years subject to<font For those tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>positions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>where the Company has<font style="color:#000000;"> </font>determined there<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>is a greater<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>than 50% likelihood<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>benefit will<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>be sustained, the Company has recorded the largest amount of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>benefit that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>may<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>potentially<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>be realized<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>upon ultimate settlement<font style="color:#000000;"> </font>with a taxing authority that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>has full knowledge<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>of<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>all<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>relevant information.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>For those income tax<font style="color:#000000;"> </font>positions<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>where it is determined there<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>is less than 50% likelihood<font style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </font>that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a tax<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>benefit will<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>be sustained, no tax benefit has been recognized.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 10. Segments</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company operates its business as one operating segment. Its chief operating decision makers, or CODMs, are its Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer. The CODMs review separate revenue information for the Company&#8217;s subscription and professional services revenue, and all other financial information presented on a consolidated basis, for purposes of making operating decisions, assessing financial performance and allocating resources.</p>

<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 11. Commitments and Contingencies</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Leases</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has entered into non-cancellable operating leases, primarily related to rental of office space and certain office equipment. Certain lease agreements include rent payment escalation clauses and free rent (rent holidays). The total amount of base rentals over the term of the leases is charged to expense using the straight-line method with the amount of the rental expense in excess of lease payments recorded as a deferred rent liability. Total rent expense for operating leases was $4.1 million, $3.8 million and $3.5 million for&#160;the&#160;years&#160;ended December&#160;31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company also finances the purchase of certain office equipment under capital lease arrangements.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other Commitments</p>

Obligations under contracts that are cancellable or with remaining terms of 12 months or less are not included.</p>

<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Apptio, Inc.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU90"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Legal Matters</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">From time to time, the Company has become involved in claims and other legal matters arising in the ordinary course of business. The Company investigates these claims as they arise. Although claims are inherently unpredictable, the Company is currently not aware of any matters that may have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s business, financial position, results of operations or cash flows, individually or in the aggregate. The Company accrues estimates for resolution of legal and other contingencies when losses are probable and estimable. As of December&#160;31, 2017, the Company does not believe that any material losses relating to claims were probable and estimable, and therefore has not recorded a reserve for any material contingencies.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 12. Credit Facilities</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On April 20, 2016, the Company amended a revolving credit agreement, or the senior credit facility, with Silicon Valley Bank. The Company was able to incur revolver borrowings on a borrowing base tied to the amount of eligible accounts receivable, not to exceed&#160;$15.0 million, under the senior credit facility. The revolver matured and expired on June 16, 2017 with no amounts outstanding. The senior credit facility was not renewed and, therefore, the Company has no active credit facilities.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 13. Subsequent Events</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On February 2, 2018, the Company acquired all outstanding membership interests of Digital Fuel SV, LLC, or Digital Fuel. The Company acquired Digital Fuel to extend its leadership of the Technology Business Market and broaden the Company&#8217;s customer base. The Company&#8217;s accounting and analysis of this transaction is pending completion. The total estimated consideration for Digital Fuel was $42.5 million, comprised of $38.3 million in cash, subject to certain post-closing adjustments provided for in the Purchase Agreement, and 176,406 shares of Apptio&#8217;s Class A common stock.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="ITEM_9A_CONTROLS_PROCEDURES"></a><a name="ITEM_9A_CONTROLS_PROCEDURES"></a>Item 9A. Controls and Procedures. </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:2.62%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our management, with the participation of our principal executive officer and principal financial officer, has evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, or the Exchange Act, as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Based on such evaluation, our principal executive officer and principal financial officer have concluded that as of such date, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:2.62%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management&#8217;s Annual Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rule 13a-15(f) under the Exchange Act). Management conducted an assessment of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting based on the criteria set forth in Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework). Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting is not intended to provide absolute assurance that a misstatement of our financial statements would be prevented or detected. Based on that assessment, management has concluded that its internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December&#160;31, 2017 to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements in accordance with GAAP. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">This Annual Report on Form 10-K does not include an attestation report of our independent registered public accounting firm. For as long as we remain an &#8220;emerging growth company&#8221; as defined in the JOBS Act, we are exempt from the requirement that our registered public accounting firm provide an attestation report on the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:2.62%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Changes in Internal Control</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There was no change in our internal control over financial reporting identified in connection with the evaluation required by Rule 13a-15(d) and 15d-15(e) of the Exchange Act that occurred during the three months ended December 31, 2017 that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are in the process of making enhancements and modifications to existing internal controls and procedures to ensure compliance with ASU 2014-09. We expect these changes to our control environment to be completed in the first quarter of 2018.</p>
